subject: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@helioshealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helioshealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)

Hi Dana + Marco,

As discussed on Tuesday, attaching our current draft consent form for the reference program / public case study.

Attachment: Redwood-Reference-Program-Consent-Form-Draft-v2.docx

A couple specific items we’d love your guidance on from a Helios compliance/legal standpoint:

1) What Helios is comfortable treating as “public” statements (e.g., “deployed in a private VPC,” “supports audit logs + KMS,” “met internal latency SLOs,” etc.).
2) Whether Helios prefers anonymization (no logo/company name) vs named attribution with a more limited set of claims.
3) Whether metrics should be excluded entirely, expressed as ranges (e.g., “~30–40% lower p95”), or allowed as exact figures.

If helpful, we can keep the initial asset “compliance-safe” (no PHI, no patient volume, no model names, no region specifics) and reserve any deeper details for private reference calls.

Could you share redlines / suggested language by EOD Fri (10/10)? Happy to hop on a quick call as well.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
GTM Ops / Programs (Legal liaison)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Dana Patel <dana.patel@helioshealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@helioshealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helioshealth.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 12:41 PM
Subject: Re: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks. We reviewed the draft at a high level and have a few areas we will need to adjust before Helios can approve anything public-facing.

Key points (summary; redlines to follow):

- “Public” statements: we need to treat any statement that could be interpreted as a security/compliance guarantee as non-public unless tightly qualified. For example, “HIPAA compliant” is not acceptable for us; we can consider “supports HIPAA-aligned controls” or “supports audit logging and customer-managed keys.”

- Anonymization: our default is to avoid using the Helios name/logo in marketing materials. There may be an exception if (a) we can limit scope to a short quote without metrics and (b) Helios has final approval of the final design/layout.

- Metrics: we will not approve exact performance/cost metrics for publication. We may consider ranges, but only if framed as “observed in our environment” and excluding baseline vendor names.

- Architecture: please avoid diagrams that show network layout, region, subnets, or references to internal tooling names.

We’ll send a redlined version of the consent form shortly.

Regards,
Dana Patel
Associate General Counsel
Helios Health


---

From: Dana Patel <dana.patel@helioshealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@helioshealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helioshealth.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 2:07 PM
Subject: Re: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)

Hi Hannah,

Sending the redlined draft.

Attachment: Helios_Redlines_ConsentForm_v2.docx

Notable edits:

1) Logo + attribution
- Changed default to “no logo / no company name” unless we explicitly check a box for named use.
- Added requirement that any public page/PDF must be approved by Helios in final form (not just copy).

2) Quotes
- Removed language permitting Redwood to “edit quotes for clarity.” We can allow minor edits only with written approval from the speaker and Helios Legal.

3) Metrics and benchmarks
- Removed section allowing numeric metrics. Added option for qualitative statements only (“reduced latency,” “improved reliability,” “lowered costs”) and a separate optional clause for ranges with pre-approval.

4) Security/compliance language
- Added a prohibition on claims implying certification/attestation unless Helios can independently verify.
- Added language that Redwood may not reference our regulatory posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC reports, etc.) in public content.

5) Term + revocation
- Shortened the term to 12 months with renewal upon mutual written agreement.
- Added a 10-business-day removal SLA upon revocation.

Let me know if you want to discuss.

Best,
Dana


---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@helioshealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helioshealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 4:18 PM
Subject: Re: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)

Dana — this is very helpful, thank you.

A few clarifications / proposed path forward based on your redlines:

1) Named vs anonymized
Understood that anonymized is the default. If we proceed anonymized, can we still state “healthcare provider” and “regulated environment,” without mentioning HIPAA or any specific regulatory framework?

2) Qualitative vs ranges
We can absolutely keep the public story qualitative. If we end up requesting ranges later, we’ll treat that as a separate addendum + explicit written approval.

3) Diagrams
We’ll exclude any network diagram for the public version. For private reference calls, we can use a simplified architecture graphic (no region, no vendor names) and treat it as confidential.

4) Quote edits
No problem — we can remove the “edit for clarity” clause, or replace it with “minor formatting changes only (punctuation/typos) with customer approval.”

Also: our Product Marketing team has a standard “claims + proof” checklist; Soojin (cc’d) can ensure the story language stays within these constraints.

If you’re open to it, I’d suggest we align on what we consider “public-safe claims” for Helios so we don’t churn cycles on drafting:

- “Deployed Redwood Private within a customer-controlled VPC” (no cloud/region)
- “Customer-managed encryption keys via KMS integration” (no vendor)
- “Audit log export supported” (format/retention details omitted)
- “Improved operational visibility using Redwood Console” (no screenshots)

Can you confirm whether the above list is acceptable in principle for a public write-up (still anonymized)?

Thanks again,
Hannah


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@helioshealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helioshealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)

Dana — jumping in quickly from Product Marketing.

We can keep the story both anonymized and “controls-focused” without compliance claims. In practice we avoid:

- “compliant with” / “certified” language
- naming specific regulatory frameworks on behalf of the customer
- implying Redwood audited Helios’ environment

We can use phrasing like:

- “Helios required a private deployment with customer-managed networking controls.”
- “The deployment supports customer-managed keys and audit logging integrations.”
- “Helios prioritized reliability with fallback policies to reduce end-user impact during capacity events.”

And we’ll include a disclaimer on the page that: “Implementation details vary by customer environment; statements reflect Helios’ configuration and are not a guarantee of results.”

Let us know if you’d like to review a one-paragraph “safe claims” block before we draft the full story.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Messaging & Narrative
Redwood Inference


---

From: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@helioshealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Patel <dana.patel@helioshealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@helioshealth.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 9, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Helios case study: consent language + compliance review (logo/quotes/metrics)

Hannah / Soojin,

Confirming the “public-safe claims” direction is acceptable if:

- Helios remains anonymized (no name/logo; no identifying screenshots; no unique environment identifiers).
- No mention of HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC, BAA, or any other regulatory language.
- No metrics (numbers) and no competitor/vendor names.
- Any reference to audit logs must be general (avoid format/retention guarantees). If you need a single sentence: “supports audit log export for compliance workflows” is ok.

We can review a 1-paragraph claims block up front and then do a final review of the page/PDF (layout included). Please allow 10 business days for final approval.

Separately: for reference calls, Helios can participate but we need a pre-brief on the topics and the prospect’s company name. We also want the ability to decline on a case-by-case basis.

Thanks,
Marco Alvarez
Director, Security & Compliance
Helios Health
